report_name: Japan Airlines Breach Exposes 92,000 Customers via IT Provider

attack_patterns.name: Trusted Relationship
attack_patterns.description: The attack vector was a supply chain compromise of a trusted third-party supplier, Amadeus IT Group, which manages Japan Airlines' passenger reservation system, to gain access to customer data.

attack_patterns.name: Data from Cloud Storage
attack_patterns.description: An unauthorized party accessed and viewed sensitive customer PII, including passport numbers, from the Amadeus passenger service system, which served as a data repository for Japan Airlines.

campaigns.name: Amadeus System Cyberattack
campaigns.description: A supply chain attack originating at Amadeus IT Group that resulted in the exposure of customer data for Japan Airlines and its subsidiary, Japan Transocean Air, between August 2023 and September 2026.

identities.name: Japan Airlines
identities.description: Primary victim of the data breach. The personal information of approximately 92,000 of its customers was exposed via a supply chain attack on its IT provider, Amadeus IT Group.

identities.name: Japan Transocean Air
identities.description: A subsidiary of Japan Airlines whose customers were also affected by the data breach originating at Amadeus IT Group.

identities.name: Amadeus IT Group
identities.description: A Spanish technology provider for JAL's passenger service system. The data breach originated within its systems, making it the vector for the supply chain attack.
